quotes.text: We curated a subset of 26 patient cases from the HANCOCK dataset (CC BY 4.0)
The **MSK-CHORD** dataset is available on [cBioPortal](https://www.cbioportal.org/study/summary?id=msk_chord_2024).

rationale: Both source datasets (HANCOCK, MSK-CHORD) are named with citations, and the README gives platforms (HANCOCK project page, cBioPortal study id). No version or snapshot date is stated and no explicit route from each question to its source record is documented, so the source is named without version or route.

quotes.text: MSK-CHORD dataset (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0)
a multimodal repository of head and neck cancer patients that includes demographic, pathological, hematological, surgical, and histological data

rationale: Origin (two public clinical datasets) and source licences (CC BY 4.0, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) are stated. No consent, IRB status or explicit statement that consent is not required appears, and no repo licence is shown in the packet. Origin plus one other element gives 1.

quotes.text: For each selected patient, an average of 40 modality-specific files are available, including 1.2 H&E slides, 26.2 IHC images, and one hematology report.

rationale: Descriptive cohort statistics are given (26 and 40 cases, files per patient, slide counts) but no comparison against a named target population, no demographic distribution and no selection rule for the subsets. Weak 1 on the descriptive-statistics branch.

searched: S1 (abstract, evaluation, societal impacts, appendices), S2 README, S3 (no chunks), S4 code and logs, S5 prompts. No unsafe-output test and no bias or fairness test is reported; the societal-impact paragraph is a statement only and file-name hallucination is logged but not presented as a safety test.

searched: S1 (dataset, Q&A design, evaluation, appendices), S2 README, S3 (no chunks), S4 config and code, S5 prompts. No gating, canary, encryption, held-out set or overlap check is reported; questions and source data are public and no contamination analysis appears.

searched: S1 (agentic workflow, appendix D.1, E), S2 README, S4 run script and config, S5 system prompts. The paper describes which files the agent may request but never states that the agent cannot reach ground-truth answers or names an isolation mechanism.

quotes.text: we use the gpt-4o-2024-08-06 checkpoint for gpt4o and the o4-mini-2025-04-16 checkpoint for o4-mini
The tool retrieves the top 30 articles from PubMed based on the provided query and reranks them using the BAAI-bge-reranker-v2-m3 model.

rationale: Question files, API checkpoints and a DrugBank snapshot are fixed, but the PubMed tool queries the live service at evaluation time and dataset versions or snapshot dates are not stated. Data pinned with a live service in the loop gives 1.

quotes.text: the final set of questions in MTBBench were sent for external manual review by domain specialists via the companion application

rationale: No scripted reference solution is run through the grader. Manual expert review of question and answer soundness (10 experts, Table 3 agreement) is the only evidence that tasks are correct and answerable, which fits the manual-evidence level.

searched: S1 (agentic workflow, tasks, appendix D.1), S2 README, S4 agent code, S5 prompts. Every task is multiple-choice or true/false question answering; file requests and tool calls only read patient data, so no task changes environment state and the NA clause applies.

quotes.text: outcome and recurrence prediction remain the most difficult, with accuracies near random (50%), even for leading models

rationale: The paper discloses that several tasks sit near chance (50% for binary tasks; six-option items are mentioned in appendix E.4) but reports no random or trivial-agent run and no per-metric chance rate for every task. Disclosed large chance rate under G5 gives 1.
searched: S1 (Tables 2, Figs 2, 3, 8 text, appendix G), S2 README, S3 (no chunks), S4 run script. No do-nothing, random or majority-class agent score is reported for any task.

searched: S1 (appendix E.4, C.2, Table 3), S2 README, S4 code. Grading is regex answer extraction with a re-prompt rule; no tests, reference solutions or error figures for the parser are reported. The inter-rater agreement in Table 3 validates question quality, not the evaluator.

quotes.text: temperature=0.2,

rationale: No seed, temperature or repeated-run policy appears in S1-S3. A fixed temperature of 0.2 is visible only in the GPT-4o harness code and covers only part of the harness (open-model eval code in the packet shows no sampling controls). Safeguards visible only in code give 1.

quotes.text: To quantify uncertainty, we estimate 95% confidence intervals using bootstrap resampling with 1000 iterations.
access to visual foundation model tools significantly improves performance on all multimodal tasks

rationale: Per-model bootstrap 95% CIs are reported in Table 2, but no test or paired CI is given for the headline comparisons (model rankings, tool versus no-tool). Statements such as 'significantly improves' carry no test, so the score is capped at 1.

searched: S1 (section 3, appendix E.4, E.5), S2 README, S3 (no chunks). No number of runs per task, no seed or decoding policy and no statement on run independence appears on S1-S3; a single run per model is implied but not stated. Temperature appears only in S4 code.

quotes.text: confidence intervals computed by resampling (with replacement) 1,000 times from the set of patient–question pairs within each task

rationale: CIs are on every headline cell and the resampling unit is stated (patient-question pairs; appendix text says question outcomes). Clustering of 15 questions within each patient (or questions within templates) is not addressed, and the resampling unit wording differs between the table caption and section 3.1.

searched: S1 (section 3, appendices D.1, E, G), S2 README, S3 (no chunks). No rerun, per-task repeat outcomes, pass^k metric, or action or state agreement across identical reruns is reported; logs are from one run per model and condition.

quotes.text: we use the gpt-4o-2024-08-06 checkpoint for gpt4o and the o4-mini-2025-04-16 checkpoint for o4-mini

rationale: The two API models carry dated snapshot ids; open models are given by family name and size (README example uses an unversioned HF id), which is partial. No decoding parameters on S1-S3 (only quantization bit-width) and no harness tag or commit matched to reported numbers.

quotes.text: the tool returns the one with highest embedding similarity to the image, based on dot product in the shared representation space
The model is allowed to access files by explicitly specifying the filename and extension in the prescribed format

rationale: Text-command protocol, so not NA. S1 documents what CONCH, PubMed, DrugBank and the IHC tool return (similarity-ranked label with confidence bin, top 3 abstracts, description) but gives no schema for every tool, no read/write side-effect statement, and no error or failure returns. S5 prompts give command formats and only say files are 'allowed to read', so side effects do not reach S5.

quotes.text: This setup simulates a realistic clinical workflow, where an agent opens several clinical files from a patient folder
You can access all these files once again if necessary by asking for them in the format [REQUEST: filename.extension].

rationale: No tests or conformance checks of the tools are reported. The only simulated behaviour is file open and close (files detached after each question), disclosed in appendix D.1 and surfaced to the agent by the detach notice in the prompt; tools themselves are real. Weak 1 because S1 never states that nothing else is simulated.

searched: S1 (agentic workflow, appendix D.1, E.4), S2 README, S4 agent code, S5 system prompts. Agent actions are file requests, tool queries and an answer choice; none changes environment state or represents an order, prescription, note or message, so the NA clause applies.

quotes.text: This formulation enables objective evaluation without relying on human annotators or oracle LLMs, thereby ensuring reproducibility and consistency across models.

rationale: Grader input is the answer string extracted by regular expressions (with up to three re-prompts), and a rationale is given for not using humans or LLM judges. No validation of the parser on labelled correct and incorrect outputs is reported; the expert agreement in Table 3 concerns question quality.

searched: S1 (tools, workflow, appendices C-E), S2 README, S3 (no chunks), S4 config and logs, S5 prompts. No control on leakage via PubMed retrieval or other tools, no private or held-out split, and no canary or provenance marker. Stage-limited file availability is a task design choice, not stated as a leakage control; per-run logs with gold answers and the questions are public in the repo.

quotes.text: Multi-Modal Analysis | Digital Pathology | Hematology | Outcome and Recurrence | Overall

rationale: Results are broken out by task family for both tracks (Table 2, Figs 3, 8). Both source datasets hold demographic fields but no per-patient-subgroup results are reported, and Table 2 gives no n per slice (per-patient question mix is described only in the design text).

quotes.text: a multimodal repository of head and neck cancer patients that includes demographic, pathological, hematological, surgical, and histological data
MSK-CHORD dataset (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0)

rationale: Records come from real patient datasets (HANCOCK, MSK-CHORD) and data licences are stated separately from code. No IRB determination, DUA or credentialing requirement, or de-identification method is described; the DrugBank licence note concerns a drug database, not patient records.
